changes.summary: Adds pkg/automation/engine, the automation engine on the workflow substrate: graph versions with layouts, Enable by a human only (code review digest, trigger read permissions, owner in trigger_owners), one outbox consumer (automations) that fans events out to enabled triggers and open waits with a cause depth limit, tenant schedules (five calendar cron fields; intervals are refused), manual starts and restarts, and the native runner of automation.run that keeps tokens, steps and waits in the new automation.* tables inside fenced transactions (parallel/join/foreach, event waits with timers, tasks and calls, conversation queues, retention). Publishes automation.run.finished.v1 and automation.run.failed.v1 once per failed run, delivered to the graph owner by the core notification definition of pkg/automation/engine/ownernotice (Contribute); outbox events gain a cause column. graph: the join and foreach outputs declare a branch's output and an item's value optional, so reading the results of a partial_failed foreach is no longer missing context.

Fixes the automation engine after review: a node's effects roll back when its output is too large, foreach keeps large integers exact, wait deadlines count from after the subject lock, run history releases its connection before projecting and hides filter_error reasons from viewers without the fields, cron with CRON_TZ=/TZ= or not five fields is refused instead of panicking, Enable locks the connections it uses and connectors Store.Delete checks uses inside its transaction through the new optional connectors.TxUsageIndex (the engine UsageIndex implements it), so the two never wait on each other for pool connections, manual starts and restarts resolve run-as under the graph lock, Restart drops retained input values whose own provenance has no access rule left, the queue recovery scan skips busy subjects, queued cancellation takes the subject lock first and changes the queue row before the run row, as promotion and Disable do, a restart that cannot run no longer supersedes its predecessor, SaveVersion/Enable/Disable answer with the state they committed, schedule activation is taken after the graph lock, and retention uses one cutoff and never cascades to kept steps.

Automation graphs: nodes are validated by the triggers that reach them (unknown_variable_for_trigger), triggers about different subjects need no mixed subject, CEL gains join(list<string>, sep), and list elements typed in Go ([]map[string]string and the like) are readable as list<map>.

Metrics band styles move to styles/tailwind/metrics.css (imported by iota.css, shipped as @iota-uz/sdk/metrics.css) so hosts with their own theme sheet can import them; table.InTablePanels is exported; the band scope line uses --clr-text-200 for contrast.
Fix golangci-lint findings on Linux-only pykernel and MCP execute files (checked Close errors, no named results, testify helpers); no behavior or public API change.

pykernel confines every Python kernel before the first instruction of user code: Landlock (ABI >= 6) limits files to read-only runtime paths and a read-write session workdir, denies TCP and scopes abstract unix sockets and signals; seccomp refuses socket creation, ptrace, namespaces, mount, bpf, keyrings, perf, io_uring, process_vm_* and setsid/setpgid; no_new_privs and an empty capability set; the shim sets AS/CPU/FSIZE/NPROC/NOFILE itself. New isolation.Check reports which boundaries are really in force (verified in a child); manager.New fails closed with the missing list (isolation.Profile{Mode: ModeInsecureDisabled} opts out for development), and every kernel must report the same boundaries in a kernel.ready handshake. New pkg/pykernel/conformance suite and cmd/pykernel-conformance for consumers. Kernels get default limits, a server wall-clock cap and a workdir quota (bytes and entries, for the kernel's whole life; Acquire returns ErrWorkdirQuota for an over-entries workdir); EventDone now carries Reason (completed/error/cancelled/timeout/quota_exceeded/kernel_exited), EventsDropped, NamespaceReset and FilesPreserved; the bridge never blocks on a stalled consumer; exec cancellation and timeouts always cancel capability calls, and calls outside the running exec are refused; Session may implement CallContextBinder for the user identity; lifecycle FreshNamespace is enforced; WarmPool evicts the LRU idle kernel at MaxParallel; reuse across tenants or modes returns ErrSessionMismatch. Breaking: the shim moves to a host-owned runtime directory and the bridge.Bridge interface gains ResetNamespace. Review hardening: every address-bearing socket call is refused; the workdir quota is enforced at allocation time by a host supervisor over seccomp user notification that performs every write-family call itself (pidfd_getfd, fixed checked offset, blocks plus entries, unlinked and mapped files charged, killable waits); no thread or process starts while no exec runs and idle CPU is budgeted; Docker deployments grant the app CAP_SYS_PTRACE or Manager.New fails closed; New rejects unknown modes and execute requires a verified Isolation() report (InsecureAllowUnconfinedRuntime opts out); MaxParallel counts in-flight spawns; the restart record is host-owned; artifacts are collected through O_NOFOLLOW directory descriptors under a per-session gate; DonePayload.Error keeps the first error under backpressure. Review round 2: the worker's exec.done is untrusted (the host ends an exec only when the kernel is at rest, killing processes the exec started; the watchdog stays armed until then); emulated writes go through the host's own description of the file; O_TMPFILE/memfd creations and held unnamed inodes are counted; host SysV IPC and POSIX mqueues are refused; isolation.Check proves the host can act for a confined process; a stopped submission returns its typed outcome; retiring kernels keep their MaxParallel slot until torn down. Review round 3: a supervised kernel is frozen (SIGSTOP, verified) whenever no exec runs, so left-behind work only resumes inside a later exec; exec-end kills go through pidfds; prlimit64/setpriority/sched_set*/ioprio_set/migrate_pages/move_pages act only on the caller; mapped-only unnamed inodes cost an entry; Wait empties the process group before reaping the leader and retiring kernels hold their slot until gone; a kernel dying during submission reports kernel_exited. QA rounds: an exec request that does not fit a bridge frame returns ErrRequestTooLarge before any state changes; freeze and rest checks rely on positive observation only; a broken bridge or submission publishes its terminal event only once the process group is gone; FreshNamespace on a confined kernel that ran code means a new process; Acquire stops waiting for a retiring group on cancellation.
pykernel: identify a session workdir by device, inode and birth time, so a recreated workdir that reuses the old inode is reported as a reset without preserved files.
